title: Unlocking AI Powered DevOps Within Your Organization — Jon Peck, GitHub
talk_summary: A GitHub developer advocate describes how to adopt AI in DevOps: IDE-integrated agents, codified repo instructions, knowledge bases, and semi-autonomous issue-to-PR agents that always work on isolated branches behind human review.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a committed instructions file in the repo that encodes team standards (linting, patterns, checks) so every AI interaction obeys it, and treat updating it as a lead's ongoing job.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's my job to make sure that ends up in the copilot instructions file. So as they're working with AI, it's keeping all those same best practices in mind.

takeaways.technique: Narrow context by folder/file scope before running
takeaways.what_they_do: Pull in only the relevant folders and settings files and have the agent first narrow context and emit a plan before editing, avoiding overloaded prompts and scope creep.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I tell it only focus on these files on these folders, then it's not going to try and do a whole bunch of other stuff I don't want it to do

takeaways.technique: Async reviewer as assignee with accept/reject suggestions
takeaways.what_they_do: Assign the AI reviewer to a PR like a human; it posts comments and suggested rewrites asynchronously that a human accepts or rejects, rather than auto-injecting changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these won't be automatically injected. They'll show up and this is our major philosophy the same way anything a human would do.

takeaways.technique: Issue-to-PR autonomous agent in isolated branch
takeaways.what_they_do: Assign a well-shaped issue to an autonomous agent that creates its own branch, works in a protected environment, and returns a PR for human review; bad results are discarded and the issue refined and reassigned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: writing a well-shaped issue the same way you would write a well-shaped prompt say focus on these do these exact things these should be the outcomes

takeaways.technique: Use AI for planning, tests, docs, and IaC before production code
takeaways.what_they_do: Apply models to planning, security scanning, test generation, deployment file generation, and documentation, which the speaker claims yields more lift than code generation alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Usually in about 10% of the time it would normally take me to build all those tests, I've got at least a functioning skeleton
takeaways.numbers: test generation ~10% of normal time (speaker's anecdote)

takeaways.what_they_do: Connect agents to a GitHub MCP server so they can branch, commit, open PRs, and assign reviewers without leaving the agent loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: put it on a new branch. Uh, go ahead and commit it with a sensible commit. Uh, and then create a new PR for it
